title: Uncle Chet the violinist and learning without teachers
summary: His uncle Chet played violin in a family group, but Bunn learned only by watching and listening; Rosenberg compares his own son's first try at guitar.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up a first guitar or banjo, self-taught

blocks.x: That's amazing. It's hard, you know -- did you have anybody, like uncles, come over and show you anything, or --
Well, I had my middle uncle, Chet.
Uh-huh.
His name was Chester. And we called him Uncle Chet, and he played violin.
Uh-huh.

And I mean he was a wonderful violinist. Chet Munn (PHONETIC). And I picked up the guitar and started playing, and they were surprised at me even trying to play, and what I could do to it when I picked it up. It was just a gift.
Huh. So did Chester play like with
Chey, yeah. He had a little group there. I forget the name of it now. It's been so long.
That must be about -- well, way back.
Yeah.
Yeah.
So he probably showed you a little bit how to hold it, or --
No, no. He didn't show me nothing. I just picked it up.
Just the example, huh?
Yeah, by looking.
Yeah.
I saw. And how I went to the guitar like I did was that I seen somebody else, you know, just sitting down, trying to play whatever they picked up to play, and they had it across their lap, you know.
Right. Strumming.
Strumming. And I just picked it up and started playing it, and they were surprised. Yeah.
Sure.
And it didn't take me but a few days to get used to it. I guess that was the gift right there.
The ears.
Yeah.
The ears. Because my son, like I remember when he first picked up my guitar -- well, I just actually had a little ukulele around.
Yeah.
And he held it just right. I mean he looked -- because kids have sharp eyes.
Yeah.
But his ear didn't tell him that much. His ear wasn't helping him out, you know.
Yeah.
But with you, it must have sounded like not only could you see what was happening, but you could hear what it should sound like.
Yeah. That's wonderful.
That's beautiful.
Sure. Well, see, he's got a gift, and you keep following that up.
Oh, yeah. Well, he likes the drums.
For your own benefit and his too.
